claims.pass_condition: Planning removes nothing and application requires the exact, structurally valid, root-bound proposal.
claims.counterevidence: Wrong, reshaped, copied-root, or implicit authority removes a source file.
claims.observed_evidence: Wrong digest, undeclared sealed field, copied root, unrequested CLI, and exact approval assertions pass.

claims.pass_condition: The named disposable workload has fewer files and fewer storage bytes after rollup, and no non-smaller target is selectable.
claims.primary_surface: pre/post deep-audit counters under the five-segment fixture
claims.counterevidence: Target bytes are equal/larger, source count does not fall, or planning selects a non-positive reduction.
claims.observed_evidence: Five-segment fixture moves from ten source files to three target files, storage bytes decrease, and candidate reduction is positive and exact.

claims.pass_condition: Final source validation and removal hold the owner lifecycle lock and reject live, busy, or changed unapproved history.
claims.counterevidence: A busy owner or newly active segment loses source history.
claims.observed_evidence: Held lock returns COORDINATION_BUSY; new active session returns STALE; both record zero removal authority.

claims.pass_condition: The current event blob reproduces every original source byte and the lineage retains all original archive and prior rollup receipts.
claims.primary_surface: lineage-aware deep audit plus direct lineage inspection
claims.counterevidence: Any receipt boundary, digest, event transition, original receipt, prior rollup receipt, or final tail is missing or inconsistent.
claims.observed_evidence: Thirty-three events validate through one rollup head; lineage contains ten original archive receipts and the prior rollup receipt with matching receipt-set digest.

claims.pass_condition: Exact replay completes both pre-anchor partial publication and post-anchor source cleanup without touching later live history.
claims.primary_surface: partial-target, restored-source, and live-cleanup recovery fixtures
claims.counterevidence: Replay conflicts with its own exact target, silently accepts extra source files, deletes changed files, or breaks the active session.
claims.observed_evidence: One prewritten target blob is reused; restored sources produce REVIEW_REQUIRED; exact replay returns RECOVERED while a later session protects and releases normally.

claims.pass_condition: A fresh process and a later rollup continue exact generation and lineage from the first rollup.
claims.primary_surface: fresh Node child process followed by new curation and repeated rollup
claims.counterevidence: Generation restarts, new history cannot be archived, or the second rollup loses the first receipt lineage.
claims.observed_evidence: Fresh child continues at generations nineteen through twenty-one; later exact curation and rollup finish with thirty-three events and one preserved prior rollup receipt.

claims.pass_condition: Deep audit detects missing or corrupted lineage, unexpected extra source files, and exceeded raw-byte ceilings while accepting the valid repeated rollup.
claims.primary_surface: auditArchives missing, same-size tamper, interruption, and budget fixtures
claims.counterevidence: Any named corruption passes or valid repeated lineage fails.
claims.observed_evidence: Valid repeated rollup is COMPLETE; missing lineage and same-size corruption are REVIEW_REQUIRED; raw byte ceiling is LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

claims.pass_condition: CLI and module declarations expose separate plan/apply routes and all four rollup schemas without broadening authority.
claims.primary_surface: CLI self-test and discovery seam review
claims.counterevidence: CLI lacks dry-run separation, schemas are undeclared, or boundaries permit automatic or lossy rollup.
claims.observed_evidence: 121 CLI checks and 53 discovery-seam checks pass with explicit measured-plan, exact-apply, no-automation, and no-history-loss declarations.

claims.pass_condition: Only derived cold containers are replaced; durable event bytes and receipts remain, and long-horizon semantic retention stays open.
claims.primary_surface: runtime authority objects, contracts, gap report, and implementation receipt
claims.counterevidence: Rollup claims history deletion, scheduling, general performance, native execution, promotion, or CANON.
claims.observed_evidence: All authority objects keep install/promotion/CANON false; contracts refuse semantic deletion; the next gap is durable-history tiering and retention.
